table.brief: On-call rotation: Week (rowspan 2) / Role (primary/secondary) / Engineer / Phone / Escalation notes

understanding.purpose: Show who is on call each week, how to reach them, and what escalation or coverage conditions apply.
understanding.reading: Readers find a week, scan its primary and secondary rows, then match each engineer and phone number to the relevant notes. The merged week cells already span two rows, so wrapped week labels can use that shared height.
groups: Week and Role establish the schedule and distinguish the two assignments within each week.
Engineer and Phone form a contact pair that readers need to match quickly.
Escalation notes provide instructions and exceptions for each assignment.
keep_intact: Phone numbers, for reliable reading and dialing
Individual name components and date ranges where space permits
may_wrap: Week labels between the week number and date range
Engineer names between given and family names
Escalation notes at natural word boundaries

preferred.name: r1C
preferred.note: Refine r0C by allowing names to wrap between components and giving the recovered width to notes. This tests whether clearer instructions and more even rows justify the narrower contact column.

preferred.name: r2B
preferred.note: Retain r1C as the notes-first reference: its three-line maximum and natural name wrapping make it the strongest current balance when compact instructions matter more than keeping date ranges together.

acceptable.name: r1B
acceptable.note: Keep full engineer names and phone numbers on one line, while giving notes more room than in r0A. Accept wrapped date ranges within the merged week cells.

acceptable.name: r2A
acceptable.note: Give the week column enough room for the longest date range while retaining wrapped names and intact phone numbers. The notes column remains wider than in r1A, testing whether clearer week labels justify some additional note wrapping.

acceptable.name: r2C
acceptable.note: Give week labels 15px more than r1C while preserving most of its notes width. This tests whether shorter date ranges can stay together without substantially increasing the height of the instructions.

acceptable.name: r3A
acceptable.note: Refine r2B by giving eight more pixels to notes. Week labels already wrap over three lines in r2B, so the narrower merged Week cells may preserve that pattern while improving note wrapping; check date breaks in the render.

acceptable.name: r3B
acceptable.note: Give Week enough width for the longest date range on one line after the week number. This makes all three week labels more consistent, at the cost of narrower notes and potentially taller rows.

acceptable.name: r3C
acceptable.note: Test a Week width just sufficient for the longest one-line label's content width, allowing the week number and date range to separate naturally if needed. Compare its date readability and note wrapping with the wider Week and notes-first alternatives.

bad.name: contrast
bad.note: The phone column is too narrow to keep numbers on one line, making contact details harder to scan and use. The wide week and engineer columns also leave too little room for the escalation notes.
bad.why: The phone column is too narrow to keep numbers on one line, making contact details harder to scan and use. The wide week and engineer columns also leave too little room for the escalation notes.

rationale: r1C and r2B are identical. They give escalation notes enough room to read in short blocks while keeping roles and phone numbers on single lines. Engineer names wrap between words, and the merged week labels still clearly group each primary and secondary pair.

general: Give space to columns according to how readers use their contents, rather than making columns equal.
Keep contact details easy to scan and avoid splitting words or identifiers.
Judge wrapping across the whole row: extra lines in one column affect the spacing of every neighboring cell.
specific: The escalation notes carry the most variable text and benefit most from the remaining width.
A two-line engineer name is a reasonable compromise because each name remains intact and the phone number stays on one line.
The merged week cells preserve the grouping even when their date ranges wrap.

tradeoffs: r3A gives the notes slightly more room, but its narrower week column creates less comfortable date breaks. Wider week columns improve some date labels at the cost of longer note blocks and taller rows.
uncertain: The ranges are conservative visual estimates, not browser-tested thresholds. They describe small independent adjustments around the preferred widths, with the remaining columns adjusted proportionally within the 644px total; exact wrapping thresholds may vary by a few pixels.

critique.good: Roles, engineer names and phone numbers remain on one line, making each assignment easy to match. Notes have enough room to read in short phrases.
critique.problems: Two of the three date ranges break across lines, while notes still occupy three or four lines and leave substantial empty space in the contact columns.
critique.cause: The 100px Week column is too narrow for the longer date ranges. The 135px Engineer column preserves every full name, but leaves only 183px for notes.

critique.good: Every date range, role, name and phone number stays intact. The week groups are particularly easy to identify.
critique.problems: The notes become a narrow, tall strip of four- and five-line entries. The resulting row heights leave large areas of empty space under the contact details and make the schedule harder to scan as a whole.
critique.cause: The 126px Week column accommodates the longest date range, but reduces Escalation notes to 157px.

critique.good: The wider notes column gives instructions a comfortable measure and makes the rows more even. Roles and phone numbers remain intact, and the compact table makes week-to-week comparison easier.
critique.problems: All three date ranges split, and several engineer names wrap. The broken dates weaken the week labels, while wrapped names make the contact pair slightly slower to scan.
critique.cause: The 85px Week column cannot hold the date ranges intact, and the 115px Engineer column cannot hold every full name.

critique.good: Week labels and date ranges are easy to scan, roles and phone numbers stay intact, and each two-row week group is clear.
critique.problems: The notes are cramped and frequently run to four lines, producing tall rows and substantial empty space in the other columns. Names also wrap despite the generous width devoted to the week column.
critique.cause: The 126px week column preserves each date range on one line, but leaves only 191px for notes. The 101px engineer column cannot hold full names on one line.

critique.good: Full names and phone numbers stay on one line, making the contact pair easy to scan. The narrower week column gives some space back to the notes.
critique.problems: Date ranges split across lines, and the notes still make several rows tall. The wide contact columns create substantial empty space below their single-line contents.
critique.cause: The 85px week column is too narrow for complete date ranges. The 135px engineer column keeps names intact, but leaves only 198px for notes.

critique.good: The wider notes column makes instructions easier to read, limits them to three lines, and gives the table a more compact rhythm. Roles and phone numbers remain intact, while names wrap at word boundaries.
critique.problems: All date ranges split, weakening the week labels as scanning anchors. The short secondary row in Week 14 also creates a somewhat uneven rhythm beside the other rows.
critique.cause: The 85px week column provides only 64px for text. The 101px engineer column wraps names, while the 232px notes column lets the Week 14 secondary note fit in two lines.

critique.good: Roles and phone numbers stay intact, and the contact pair is easy to follow across each row. Week 15 and Week 16 date ranges fit on one line.
critique.problems: Week 14 leaves its final day alone on a third line. The notes are narrow enough to make two assignments four lines tall, producing a long table and substantial empty space in the other columns.
critique.cause: The 110px Week column is just too narrow for the longest date range; the 207px notes column forces additional wrapping.

critique.good: The wider notes column keeps every instruction to three lines or fewer and gives the secondary Week 14 assignment a shorter row. Roles and phone numbers remain intact, with no mid-word splits.
critique.problems: All three date ranges break across two lines, making week labels harder to scan. Names consistently occupy two lines, although they remain readable.
critique.cause: The 85px Week column leaves only 64px for text; the 101px Engineer column leaves 80px, enough for individual name components but not full names.

critique.good: Week 15's date range stays together, and roles and phone numbers remain intact. Notes have a little more room than in r2A.
critique.problems: Week 14 and Week 16 date ranges break, and the final note still needs four lines. The intermediate Week width consumes space without consistently keeping dates together.
critique.cause: The 100px Week column is wide enough for the shortest date range but not the others; the 217px notes column is still too narrow for the final instruction to fit in three lines.

review.method: two fresh-context blind reviews; letters shuffled; includes browser auto layout and equal widths as neutral references

ref_equal.why: Equal widths leave the notes cramped and tall, while role and week have spare space. Phone numbers and one engineer name wrap.

r2A.why: Phone numbers stay intact and notes have useful width, but every engineer name wraps and the first date breaks awkwardly before its final day.

ref_auto.why: The wide notes column reads comfortably, but all phone numbers wrap and the narrow week column fragments date ranges.

r1C.why: Phone numbers stay intact and notes read well, but every engineer name wraps and the week dates need three lines.

contrast.why: Weeks and engineer names are easy to scan, and notes have reasonable space. Every phone number wraps, which matters in an on-call schedule.

r1B.why: Engineer names and phone numbers stay intact, and the notes remain readable. The narrow week column breaks each date range across two lines.

raw.unsure: The trade-off between F and E depends on whether intact phone numbers or more compact week labels matter more to readers; for an on-call schedule, I favor intact phone numbers.

r2A.why: Phone numbers stay intact and notes have usable space, but every engineer name wraps and the first date range breaks awkwardly before the final day.

ref_equal.why: The narrow notes column produces long stacks of short lines, while phone numbers break across lines and the wide role column leaves substantial unused space.

r1B.why: Names and phone numbers stay on one line, and notes remain readable. The narrow week column splits every date range across lines, weakening the group labels.

ref_auto.why: Notes have generous space, but every phone number wraps, several names wrap, and the date ranges are fragmented.

r1C.why: Phone numbers stay intact and notes have comfortable line lengths. All engineer names wrap, and the date ranges split across multiple lines.

contrast.why: Week labels and engineer names stay intact, and the notes are readable. Every phone number wraps, making the numbers slower to scan and use.

raw.unsure: C preserves the engineer names and phone numbers at the expense of date-range continuity; E and F are reasonable alternatives depending on which fields readers consult most.

provenance.note: AI visual design judgement; not a human reading study
